title: Direct Observation of Dipolar-Driven Anisotropic Quantum Projection Noise in a Solid-State Spin Ensemble
authors: Tasuku Ono, Weijie Wu, Haopu Yang, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Benjamin Brenner, Che Liu, Collin Fan, Chris R. Laumann, Jonathan N. Hallén, Emily J. Davis, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, Norman Y. Yao
abstract: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is a prominent quantum-sensing platform. Combining readout at the quantum projection noise limit with strong dipolar interactions promises substantial gains in sensitivity. However, experimentally accessing this regime has remained a longstanding challenge. In this work, we demonstrate quantum-projection-noise-resolved readout of a strongly-interacting, two-dimensional ensemble of NV centers. Our approach leverages repetitive readout via the NV's intrinsic $^{15}$N nuclear memory at a moderate magnetic field ($\sim 0.3$ T), improving the readout fidelities by nearly an order of magnitude. This enables us to directly resolve the quantum projection noise of a coherent spin state and to watch the ensemble's intrinsic dipolar interactions shear this noise into an anisotropic profile. Our results open the door to direct measurements of spin squeezing and entanglement-enhanced sensing in the solid state.
summary: The research reports on achieving quantum-projection-noise-limited readout in a dense ensemble of NV centers in diamond. By using nuclear spin memory, they significantly improved readout fidelity, enabling the direct measurement of QPN. The key finding is the observation that intrinsic dipolar interactions cause the QPN to develop a measurable anisotropic profile, paving the way for solid-state entanglement sensing.
main_problem: The primary goal was to directly observe and characterize the quantum projection noise (QPN) in a strongly-interacting, two-dimensional ensemble of solid-state spins, specifically quantifying how intrinsic dipolar interactions modify this noise profile.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated QPN-resolved readout and directly observed that the dipolar interactions shear the QPN into a measurable anisotropic profile, opening pathways for solid-state entanglement sensing.
method: The measurement technique involved leveraging repetitive readout via the NV's nuclear spin memory to reach the quantum projection noise limit, followed by measuring the time-dependent variance of the collective spin operator along different axes.
model_or_system: The system is a dense, strongly interacting ensemble of Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, confined to a thin 2D layer. The dynamics are governed by dipolar interactions, which are analyzed using the collective spin Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Residual variance ($\sigma^2_{	ext{res}}$), Quantum Projection Noise ($\sigma^2_{	ext{QPN}}$), and the angular dependence of the noise ($\sigma^2_{	ext{res}}(t, \phi)$).
important_parameters: Readout noise ($\sigma_R$), number of spins ($N$), dipolar coupling strength ($J_0$), and the sensing time ($T_{	ext{sense}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that readout imperfections contribute isotropically to the measured variance, allowing the measured anisotropy to be attributed solely to the spin dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the improvement in readout fidelity via repetitive readout, the characteristic twice-per-Rabi-cycle oscillation of QPN, and the time evolution of the noise anisotropy, showing the shearing effect of dipolar interactions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the necessity of high-fidelity readout (using nuclear memory) to demonstrating the QPN signature, and finally, analyzing the time evolution of the noise variance to isolate and characterize the dipolar-induced anisotropy.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial experimental realization of measuring collective quantum noise in a solid-state platform, directly linking fundamental many-body interactions (dipolar coupling) to measurable quantum metrological signatures (noise anisotropy).
